metadata.title: Distribution of Eigenvalues for Some Sets of Random Matrices
metadata.authors: V. A. Marčenko and L. A. Pastur
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json lists short_name 'Wigner / Marchenko-Pastur', authors 'Wigner, Marchenko, Pastur', year '1955'. Actual PDF is Marčenko & Pastur (1967), Math. USSR-Sbornik 1, 457; no Wigner co-authorship. Wigner [4] is only cited as a reference.

nodes.name: Random self-adjoint operator $B_N(n)$
nodes.statement: For $A_N$ a non-random self-adjoint operator on the $N$-dimensional unitary space $H_N$, define $B_N(n) = A_N + \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i\, q^{(i)}(\cdot, q^{(i)})$, where the $\tau_i$ are i.i.d. real random variables and $q^{(i)}$ are mutually independent random vectors in $H_N$, independent of the $\tau_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: The studied random self-adjoint operator: a deterministic operator plus a sum of n independent random rank-one operators.

nodes.name: Normalized spectral function $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$
nodes.statement: $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$ is the ratio of the number of eigenvalues of $B_N(n)$ less than $\lambda$ to the dimension $N$ of the space; it is non-decreasing, left-continuous and piecewise constant in $\lambda$, with $0 \le \nu(\lambda; B_N) \le 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: The empirical eigenvalue distribution function of the operator, normalized by dimension.

nodes.name: Concentration $c$
nodes.statement: The concentration is the limit $c = \lim_{N \to \infty} n/N$, assumed to exist (Condition I).
nodes.statement_clean: The asymptotic ratio between the number of rank-one perturbations n and the dimension N.

nodes.name: Conditions I–IV on $A_N$, $q^{(i)}$, $\tau_i$
nodes.statement: (I) $\lim_{N\to\infty} n/N = c$ exists; (II) $\nu(\lambda; A_N) \to \nu_0(\lambda)$ at all continuity points; (III) the random vectors $q$ have absolute moments up to fourth order with $M q_i \bar q_j = N^{-1}\delta_{ij} + a_{ij}(N)$ and $M q_i \bar q_j q_l \bar q_m = N^{-2}(\delta_{ij}\delta_{lm} + \delta_{im}\delta_{jl}) + \varphi_{il}(N)\varphi_{jm}(N) + b_{ijlm}(N)$ with prescribed decay; (IV) the $\tau_i$ are i.i.d. with distribution $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standing hypotheses for the convergence theorem: ratio limit, deterministic-spectrum limit, vector moment conditions, and i.i.d. coefficients.

nodes.name: Stieltjes transform $m(z; c)$
nodes.statement:
$m(z; c) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}  rac{d
u(\lambda; c)}{\lambda - z}$, with inversion formula $
u(\lambda_2; c) - 
u(\lambda_1; c) = \lim_{\eta 	o +0}  rac{1}{\pi} \int_{\lambda_1}^{\lambda_2} \mathrm{Im}\, m(\xi + i\eta; c)\, d\xi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stieltjes transform of the limit spectral measure together with its inversion formula recovering the measure.

nodes.name: Generalized inverse $\tau(\xi)$ of $\sigma$
nodes.statement: For the distribution $\sigma(x)$ of the random variable $\tau$, define $\tau(\xi) = \inf\{x : \sigma(x) > \xi\}$ for $\xi \in (0,1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quantile (left-continuous generalized inverse) of the coefficient distribution.

nodes.name: Empirical distribution $\sigma(x, T_n)$ and its inverse $\tau(\xi, T_n)$
nodes.statement: Given a realization $T_n = (\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n)$ ordered $\tau_1 \le \tau_2 \le \cdots \le \tau_n$, the experimental distribution $\sigma(x, T_n)$ takes value $i/n$ on $[\tau_i, \tau_{i+1})$. Its generalized inverse is $\tau(\xi, T_n) = \tau_{i+1}$ for $\xi \in [i/n, (i+1)/n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The empirical distribution function of a sample of n coefficients, together with its quantile function.

nodes.name: Auxiliary function $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n)$
nodes.statement: For each realization $(T_n, Q_n)$ define a piecewise-linear-in-$\xi$ family interpolating the resolvent traces along the chain $B_N(i)$: $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n) = N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\, R_z(i) + nN^{-1}\{\mathrm{Sp}\, R_z(i+1) - \mathrm{Sp}\, R_z(i)\}(\xi - i/n)$ for $\xi \in [i/n, (i+1)/n]$.
nodes.statement_clean: An interpolating family of resolvent traces along the chain of operators built one rank-one perturbation at a time.

nodes.name: Marčenko–Pastur theorem (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement:
Under Conditions I–IV, (1) the spectral functions $
u(\lambda; B_N(n))$ converge in probability to a non-decreasing function $
u(\lambda; c)$ at all continuity points, with $
u(\pm\infty; c) = 
u_0(\pm\infty)$; (2) its Stieltjes transform $m(z; c)$ equals $u(z, 1)$ where $u(z, t)$ solves the functional equation $u(z, t) = m_0(z) - c \int_0^t  rac{	au(\xi) u(z,\xi)}{1 + 	au(\xi) u(z,\xi)} d\xi$; (3) the solution exists and is unique, and $u$ also satisfies the first-order PDE $u_t' - c\, 	au(t) u\, u_z' / (1 + 	au(t) u) = 0$, with implicit characteristic representation.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the four conditions, the empirical spectral measure converges in probability to a deterministic limit whose Stieltjes transform is the unique solution of an integral / first-order PDE in two variables.
assumptions: $A_N$ self-adjoint, $q^{(i)}$ random vectors, $\tau_i$ i.i.d. with distribution $\sigma$
conclusions: $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n)) \to \nu(\lambda; c)$ in probability at continuity points
$m(z; c) = u(z, 1)$ where $u(z, t) = m_0(z) - c\int_0^t \frac{\tau(\xi)\, u(z,\xi)}{1 + \tau(\xi)\, u(z,\xi)}\, d\xi$
Existence and uniqueness of the solution; equivalent first-order PDE $u_t' = c\, \tau(t)\, u\, u_z'/(1+\tau(t) u)$
Implicit form $\int_0^t \tau(\xi) u(z,\xi)\, d\xi$ relates $u$ to $m_0$ via characteristics

nodes.name: Self-consistent Stieltjes equation (1.14)
nodes.statement: Setting $t = 1$ in the integral form gives $m(z; c)\bigl(\, z + c \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{x\, d\sigma(x)}{1 + x\, m(z; c)} \bigr) = -1$, the closed self-consistent equation for the limit Stieltjes transform when $\nu_0$ corresponds to $A_N = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: The closed-form self-consistent equation (1.14) determining the Stieltjes transform of the limit spectrum.

nodes.name: Sum of equally probable projections (Example 1)
nodes.statement: For $B_N(n) = \tau \sum_{i=1}^n P_i$ with $P_i$ rank-one projections onto independent uniform unit vectors and constant $\tau$, the limit spectrum has density $\frac{d\nu}{d\lambda} = \frac{\sqrt{4 c \tau^2 - (\lambda - c\tau - \tau)^2}}{2\pi c \tau \lambda}$ on $[\lambda_-, \lambda_+]$ with $\lambda_\pm = \tau(1 \pm \sqrt{c})^2$, plus a point mass $(1-c)\delta(\lambda)$ for $0 < c < 1$. As $c \to \infty$ this reproduces Wigner's semicircle law.
nodes.statement_clean: The Marčenko–Pastur density for sums of i.i.d. rank-one projections, supported on $[\tau(1-\sqrt c)^2, \tau(1+\sqrt c)^2]$ plus an atom at zero.

nodes.name: Random projections with bounded random coefficients (Example 2)
nodes.statement: For $B_N(n) = \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i P_i$ with $\tau_i$ density $[\pi(1-\tau^2)^{1/2}]^{-1}$ on $(-1,1)$ and $A_N = 0$, equation (1.14) yields $z^2 m^4 + 2(1-c) z m^3 + ((1-c)^2 - z^2) m^2 - 2z(1-c) m - 1 + 2c = 0$. For $c = 1$ it reduces to a biquadratic, giving an explicit density supported on $[-2, 2]$.
nodes.statement_clean: An explicit example with arcsine-distributed coefficients producing a quartic algebraic equation for the Stieltjes transform.

nodes.name: Random projections with unbounded (Cauchy) coefficients (Example 3)
nodes.statement: For $\tau_i$ Cauchy with density $\pi^{-1} a/(a^2 + \tau^2)$, equation (1.14) becomes $m = -1/(z\,(1 - i a c/(1 - i a m)))$, a quadratic whose solution gives a limit measure supported on the entire real axis.
nodes.statement_clean: An unbounded-coefficient example showing the limit spectrum can occupy the whole real line.

nodes.name: Edge–density rule applied to Example 1
nodes.statement: Applying the edge-determination procedure to (1.18) $z = -1/m + c \tau / (1 + \tau m)$ gives extrema $m_\pm = -(1/\tau)(1 \pm 1/\sqrt{c})$, hence edges $\lambda_\pm = \tau(1 \pm \sqrt{c})^2$, and the second derivatives confirm the square-root singularity $d\nu/d\lambda \propto |\lambda - \lambda_\pm|^{1/2}$ at the edges.
nodes.statement_clean: The general edge-finding rule, applied to Example 1, recovers the Marčenko–Pastur edges and square-root vanishing.

nodes.name: Edge equation (1.16) and singularity formula (1.17)
nodes.statement: If $\alpha$ is the endpoint of an interval where the right-hand side $x(m; c)$ of (1.15) is monotonically increasing, then $\lambda_\alpha = x(\alpha; c)$ is a connected-component endpoint of the spectrum, and locally $d\nu(\lambda; c)/d\lambda \sim \bigl(\frac{2k}{(2k)!\, x^{(2k)}(\alpha)}\bigr)^{1/(2k)} \bigl|\lambda - \lambda_\alpha\bigr|^{(2k-1)/(2k)}$ where $2k$ is the order of the first non-vanishing derivative of $x(m; c)$ at $\alpha$.
nodes.statement_clean: Procedure for locating spectrum boundaries and describing the algebraic singularities of the density at those boundaries.

nodes.name: Quadratic-form concentration (Lemma 1)
nodes.statement: If the random vector $q = (q_1, \ldots, q_N)$ obeys Condition III, then $M\bigl|(A q, q) - N^{-1} \mathrm{Sp}\, A\bigr| \le \|A\|\, \varepsilon(N)$ where $\varepsilon(N) \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$ and does not depend on the operator $A$.
nodes.statement_clean: The random quadratic form $(A q, q)$ concentrates around the normalized trace $N^{-1}\,\mathrm{Sp}\, A$, uniformly over $A$.

nodes.name: Resolvent rank-one perturbation identity (Lemma 2)
nodes.statement: Let Hermitian $A, \tilde A$ on $H_N$ be related by $\tilde A = A + \tau (\cdot, q) q$ with $q$ obeying Condition III. Then $\mathrm{Sp}\, \tilde R_z - \mathrm{Sp}\, R_z = -\frac{d}{dz} \log[1 + \tau (R_z q, q)] = -\frac{\tau (R_z^2 q, q)}{1 + \tau (R_z q, q)} = -\frac{\tau N^{-1}\,\mathrm{Sp}\, R_z^2}{1 + \tau N^{-1}\,\mathrm{Sp}\, R_z} + \delta(z, q, N)$, where the random remainder satisfies $M|\delta(z, q, N)| \le |y|^{-1}(1 + |\tau||y|^{-1}) \varepsilon(N)$ with $z = x + iy$.
nodes.statement_clean: Trace-of-resolvent perturbation formula for a rank-one update of a Hermitian operator, with a vanishing-in-N stochastic remainder.
assumptions: Hermitian $A, \tilde A$ with $\tilde A = A + \tau (\cdot, q) q$
conclusions: $\mathrm{Sp}\,\tilde R_z - \mathrm{Sp}\, R_z = -\frac{\tau N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\, R_z^2}{1 + \tau N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\, R_z} + \delta(z,q,N)$

nodes.name: $L^1$-convergence of empirical quantile (Lemma 3)
nodes.statement: If the distribution $\sigma(x)$ has a finite first absolute moment, then almost surely $\int_0^1 |\tau(\xi, T_n) - \tau(\xi)|\, d\xi \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Almost-sure convergence of the empirical quantile function to the population quantile in the $L^1[0,1]$ metric — the inverse of Glivenko–Cantelli.

nodes.name: Mean-zero of the auxiliary functional (Lemma 4)
nodes.statement: Assume Conditions I–IV and the boundedness $|\tau| \le T$ (eq. (3.0)). For $G$ a bounded set in $\{\mathrm{Im}\, z > 3T\}$, the expectation $M\varphi_N$, where $\varphi_N = \sup_{\xi, z}\bigl| u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n) - m_0(z) + c \int_0^\xi \frac{\tau(\zeta) u_z'}{1 + \tau(\zeta) u}\, d\zeta \bigr|$, satisfies $\lim_{N\to\infty} M\varphi_N = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: The discrepancy of the auxiliary interpolant from the integral equation vanishes in expectation as $N \to \infty$ when the coefficients are bounded.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the integral equation (Lemma 5)
nodes.statement: Equation (3.17) (the integral equation $u(z, t) = m_0(z) - c \int_0^t \frac{\tau(\xi) u(z,\xi)}{1+\tau(\xi) u(z,\xi)}\, d\xi$) cannot have two distinct solutions in the class $K(\tau, z_0, R)$ of holomorphic-in-$z$, continuous-in-$(z,t)$ functions with positive imaginary part.
nodes.statement_clean: The integral functional equation governing the limit Stieltjes transform admits at most one solution in the natural function class.
assumptions: $u_1, u_2 \in K(\tau, z_0, R)$ both solve (3.17)
conclusions: $u_1 \equiv u_2$ in the cylinder $0 \le t \le 1$, $|z - z_0| < R$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5 (uniqueness via Haar's method)
nodes.statement: Adapting Haar's uniqueness method: assume two solutions, take the supremum $\xi_0$ where they agree, and derive a contradiction by maximizing $e^{-2Lt} v(z,t)$ on a cone and applying Cauchy's derivative estimate.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard Haar-style argument: suppose two solutions diverge past a critical $\xi_0$ and contradict the maximum modulus on a small cone of analyticity.

nodes.name: Set up critical $\xi_0$
nodes.statement: Let $\xi_0$ be the supremum of $\xi \in [0,1]$ such that $u_1(z,t) = u_2(z,t)$ for all $|z - z_0| < R$ and $t \in [0, \xi]$. Suppose for contradiction $\xi_0 < 1$.

nodes.name: Derive integral identity for difference $v$
nodes.statement: Set $v = u_1 - u_2$; from (3.17), $v(z, t) = -c \int_{\xi_0}^t [A(z,\xi) v(z,\xi) + B(z,\xi) v_z'(z,\xi)]\, d\xi$ for $\xi_0 \le t$, where $A, B$ are holomorphic and bounded on a cylinder $|z - z_0| \le R/2$.

nodes.name: Maximum modulus on a cone
nodes.statement: Restrict to the cone $\xi_0 \le t \le \xi_0 + H$, $|z - z_0| \le R - (1+L)(t - \xi_0)$ and consider $e^{-2Lt} v(z,t)$, which attains a positive maximum at some $(z_1, t_1)$ in the cone.

nodes.name: Contradiction via Cauchy derivative estimate
nodes.statement: Choosing $\alpha = -\beta\, e^{i\theta_0}$ along the gradient and using Cauchy's formula for $v_z'$ gives $|e^{-2L(t_1 - s)} v(z_1 - \alpha s, t_1 - s)| > |e^{-2L t_1} v(z_1, t_1)|$ for small $s > 0$, contradicting the maximum. Hence $\xi_0 = 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (bounded $\tau$ case and limit extension)
nodes.statement: Build the chain of operators (3.1), introduce the interpolant $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n)$, prove compactness from resolvent estimates, identify any limit as a solution of (3.17) via Lemmas 1–4, conclude uniqueness by Lemma 5, derive convergence in probability of $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$, and finally remove the boundedness on $\tau$ by truncation in §5.
nodes.statement_clean: Outline: chain construction, compactness, identification of the limit equation, uniqueness, then weak convergence, with truncation to remove the boundedness assumption.

nodes.name: Build chain of operators $B_N(i)$
nodes.statement: Order the realisation by $\tau_1 \le \cdots \le \tau_n$ and define $B_N(i) = A_N + \sum_{\alpha=1}^i \tau_\alpha q^{(\alpha)}(\cdot, q^{(\alpha)})$, with resolvents $R_z(i)$. Form the interpolant $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n)$ by (3.2).

nodes.name: Compactness of $\{u\}$ and $\{u_z'\}$
nodes.statement: From the resolvent bounds $\|R_z\| \le |y|^{-1}$ and (3.4)–(3.8) the families $\{u(z,\xi;N,T_n,Q_n)\}$ and $\{u_z'(z,\xi;N,T_n,Q_n)\}$ are uniformly bounded and equicontinuous on $\xi \in [0,1]$, $z$ in any bounded subset of the upper half-plane; hence relatively compact.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 to perturbation step
nodes.statement: Since $B_N(i+1) - B_N(i) = \tau_{i+1} q^{(i+1)}(\cdot, q^{(i+1)})$ is rank one, Lemma 2 applies, giving (3.11): $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n) = u(z, i/n; \ldots) - \frac{1}{n} \frac{\tau_{i+1} N^{-1} \mathrm{Sp}\, R_z^2(i)}{1 + \tau_{i+1} N^{-1} \mathrm{Sp}\, R_z(i)} \theta_i(\xi) + N^{-1}\theta_i(\xi)\delta_i$, with $\theta_i \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Replace $\tau(\xi, T_n)$ by $\tau(\xi)$ via Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Use formula (2.9), $\tau_{i+1} = \tau(\xi, T_n)$ on $[i/n, (i+1)/n]$, and Lemma 3 to replace the empirical quantile by $\tau(\xi)$ at the cost of an $L^1$ error tending to zero a.s. Combined with Lemma 4 this yields $\lim_{N\to\infty} M\,\varphi_N = 0$.

nodes.name: Pass to subsequential limit and identify it via Lemma 5
nodes.statement: By compactness extract a subsequence on which $u(z, t; N', T_n, Q_n) \to u(z, t)$; the limit satisfies the integral equation (3.17). By Lemma 5 this solution is unique, so the full sequence converges in probability.

nodes.name: Convergence of spectral functions (Helly + inversion)
nodes.statement:
By Helly's selection theorem extract a weakly convergent subsequence $
u(\lambda; B_{N'}(n')) 	o 
u'(\lambda)$; matching Stieltjes transforms via $u(z, 1)$ and the inversion formula (1.8) yields $
u(\lambda; c)$, with $
u(\pm\infty; c) = 
u_0(\pm\infty)$. Convergence in probability of the increments (4.5) and the tail bound (4.6) follow by Chebyshev.

nodes.name: Truncation to remove boundedness of $\tau$
nodes.statement: Define truncated coefficients $\tau_i^T = \tau_i \mathbf{1}_{|\tau_i| \le T}$ and the corresponding chain $B_N^T(i)$. The bound $|\nu(\lambda; B_N(i)) - \nu(\lambda; B_N^T(i))| \le \frac{1}{N}\{n[\sigma(-T, T_n) + 1 - \sigma(T, T_n)]\}$ together with the bounded-case result and Glivenko's theorem lets $T \to \infty$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Theorem 2: Hermitian matrices with continuous coefficient profile
nodes.statement: For Hermitian $B_N(n)$ built from independent unit vectors $q^{(i)}$ and a continuous function $r(t)$ with $\sup r(t) > -1$, under Conditions I–III the empirical spectra converge in probability to a $\nu(\lambda; c)$ whose Stieltjes transform $u(z, 1)$ solves $u_t' - c\, \alpha(t) u\, u_z'/(1 - \alpha(t)\, u) = 0$ with $\alpha(t) = |r(t)|^2/(1 + |r(t)|^2)$ and $u(z, 0) = m_0(z)$. The unique solution has the implicit characteristic form $u(z, t) = z^{-1} w\, m_0(w)$, where $w = z \exp\!\bigl(c \int_0^t \frac{1}{1 - \alpha(\xi)\, w\, m_0(w)}\, d\xi\bigr)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalisation of Theorem 1 to a continuous coefficient profile $r(t)$ with implicit characteristic representation of the limit.
conclusions: Stieltjes transform $u(z, 1)$ uniquely solves the stated PDE

nodes.name: Theorem 3: Random unitary matrices
nodes.statement: For unitary $U_N(n) = V_N \prod_k [(I - P_k) + P_k \exp(i\, r(k/n))]$ with $V_N$ non-random unitary, $r$ continuous on $[0, 2\pi]$, and $P_k$ projections onto independent unit vectors, under Conditions I and III the spectral functions converge in probability to a $\nu(\lambda; c)$ whose transform $n(z; c)$ solves a first-order PDE $n_t' = (2 z^{-1}/(\partial \ldots))$ with explicit characteristic representation involving $r$.
nodes.statement_clean: Companion theorem for random unitary matrices: spectral functions converge to a deterministic limit characterised by a PDE/implicit equation.
conclusions: Unique solution PDE / implicit characteristic formula for the unitary-spectrum transform

nodes.name: Wigner semicircle law (cited)
nodes.statement: For a Gaussian set of random matrices, the normalized spectral function converges as $N \to \infty$ to the semicircle distribution with density $\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4 - \lambda^2}$ on $[-2, 2]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Wigner's classical semicircle law for the limit eigenvalue density of Gaussian symmetric matrices.

nodes.name: Glivenko–Cantelli theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: As $n \to \infty$ the empirical distribution function $\sigma(x, T_n)$ almost surely converges uniformly on the entire real line to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The classical uniform law of large numbers for the empirical CDF.
nodes.origin_citation: Gnedenko, Course in the theory of probability

nodes.name: Connection to Wigner via central limit theorem
nodes.statement: As $c \to \infty$ the Marčenko–Pastur density of Example 1 reduces to Wigner's semicircle law: $K_N(n) = N^{-1/2} \sum_i (\sqrt{N}\,\tau\,q^{(i)} q^{(i)*} - \tau/N)$ is a sum of i.i.d. matrices, so by the central limit theorem its distribution is asymptotically Gaussian when $n \gg N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Heuristic CLT explanation of why the dense ($c \to \infty$) limit recovers Wigner's semicircle.

nodes.name: Three relaxations of the hypotheses
nodes.statement:
(1) $
u(\pm \infty; c) = 
u_0(\pm \infty)$ measure relative numbers of eigenvalues escaping to $\pm\infty$; (2) Condition I can be replaced by convergence in probability of $
u(\lambda; A_N)$ when $A_N$ is random independent of $	au, q$; (3) the unique solution of (1.13) is also obtained by successive approximations preserving positive imaginary part.
nodes.statement_clean: Three useful extensions / relaxations of the hypotheses of Theorem 1 stated after the proof.
